summary: Proposed on 2026-10-12 and awaiting review, ADR-013 gives the scene's nine wings, and the tabs each one opens, slots in the one slot registry that theme packages already use. Until now a theme could restyle the Control Booth, Cast, Prompting, World, Final Cut, Props, AI, Stage and Context wings through named parts but could not add an image or a line of text to any of them, and the registry and permission audit recorded that as a model gap. The registry gains 29 ids, scene.wing.<wing> and scene.wing.<wing>.<tab>, each with exactly one literal render point that theme-slot.test.tsx enforces in both directions. Slot meaning and limits do not change: data only, one to four items per slot, 24 per package, nothing drawn when empty, no code, and no access to scene data. A slot is not the protected layer and cannot press or read a wing's controls.

sections.title: Context
sections.summary: A theme package may place static images and plain text in 11 named slots, all on app pages and the scene backdrop and composer. The scene's wings are where a scene is set up, and a theme could restyle them through parts but could not add content to any of them. This is a gap in the model, not a defect, and a hand-rolled substitute is the wrong fix.

sections.title: Decision
sections.summary: slot-registry.ts stays the one list and parseSlots the one parser, gaining 29 ids: scene.wing.<wing> for each of nine wings and scene.wing.<wing>.<tab> for each tab. Each id has one literal ThemeSlot render point, and theme-slot.test.tsx fails when an id has none or a wing or tab has no id. Limits and meaning are unchanged: data only, one to four items per slot, 24 per package, nothing drawn when empty, no code and no scene data. A slot id survives component renames.

sections.title: Consequences
sections.summary: A theme can brand or annotate any wing without touching its controls. A slot is not the protected layer and holds no behavior, so it cannot press or read anything in a wing. The 24-item package cap is unchanged, so more ids do not let a package draw more. Adding a wing or tab means adding its ids and one render point, which the test enforces.
